definition: Acrimony means bitterness and angry ill will between people.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word acrimony. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know acrimony should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The band's farewell tour was canceled when decades of acrimony between the two founding members finally boiled over.
Friction is the mild, workaday version — colleagues who rub each other the wrong way but still cooperate; it stops well short of acrimony's open bitterness.
Animosity goes further than acrimony: acrimony sours the words people exchange, while animosity is settled hatred that persists even in silence.

Bitterness is the everyday word for a soured, resentful feeling, and one person can nurse it alone for years. Acrimony is mutual and out in the open: bitterness traded between people, sharpening the words on both sides of a long dispute.

Venom is hatred concentrated into a single cutting remark or look — poison delivered in one strike. Acrimony is the lasting state between people that keeps producing such strikes; a feud steeped in acrimony spits venom again and again.

Spite is a petty urge to wound — keying a car, withholding a favor — and it needs no open quarrel at all. Acrimony implies a history of real, open conflict between two parties: bitterness earned across a long dispute, not small private malice.

In everyday speech, 'bad blood' or 'bitterness' does the job; reach for acrimony in writing about disputes — divorces, lawsuits, band breakups — where the ill will itself is the story.
